\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{শসা} (shôsā)}{শসা (shôsā)}]{\bn{শসা} (shôsā) — a cucumber}

\label{lesson:BN-C232-shosa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for fine flour, then the Bengali for semolina.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{শসা}}
\textbf{\bn{শসা}} — \emph{shôsā} — \textquotedblleft{}a cucumber\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \textbf{\bn{শসা}} (\emph{shôsā}) is not settled: CDIAL has no entry for it in this sense, and a search by the gloss \textquotedblleft{}cucumber\textquotedblright{} finds only words of other shapes, such as Bengali \emph{khirā} (CDIAL 3697).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ভুট্টা} (bhuṭṭā)}{ভুট্টা (bhuṭṭā)}]{\bn{ভুট্টা} (bhuṭṭā) — maize, a corn cob}

\label{lesson:BN-C232-bhutta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a cucumber, then the Bengali for a mushroom.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ভুট্টা}}
\textbf{\bn{ভুট্টা}} — \emph{bhuṭṭā} — \textquotedblleft{}maize, a corn cob\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ভুট্টা}} (\emph{bhuṭṭā}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{bhṛṣṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}fried, roasted\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9594). CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{bhuṭā}, \textquotedblleft{}maize cob\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ছোলা} (chholā)}{ছোলা (chholā)}]{\bn{ছোলা} (chholā) — chickpeas}

\label{lesson:BN-C232-chhola}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a mushroom, then the Bengali for maize.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ছোলা}}
\textbf{\bn{ছোলা}} — \emph{chholā} — \textquotedblleft{}chickpeas\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ছোলা}} (\emph{chholā}) probably belongs with \emph{*chōll}, \textquotedblleft{}to peel, skin\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs and reports Burrow as taking from Dravidian (CDIAL 5073). Under it CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{cholā}, \textquotedblleft{}to skin\textquotedblright{}, and Oriya \emph{cholā}, \textquotedblleft{}gram\textquotedblright{}, which it explains, with a query, as \textquotedblleft{}husked\textquotedblright{}. It has no Bengali row for the pulse itself.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}
